status_note: Draft coding of 2 November 2026 (later). Not graded yet. Since 0.9.1: the four S.D.N.Y. orders whose free RECAP copies have no usable text layer were OCR'd and coded from the OCR text (R11); one of them (Sarris) takes software that runs entirely on the defense's own systems out of its definition of an AI tool (R12). Two civil orders have no free copy at the source and are final as not codable (Campbell, Elgin). Two more are being read at the source (Fischman: a free copy of the protective order was found; Dunn: only the order granting the motion is free), and Velez's provisos are being copied in full.
add_rules: R11. An order whose free RECAP copy has no usable text layer (pypdf returns only the CM/ECF stamp, or unreadable characters) is coded from OCR text: pages rendered at 300 dpi grayscale by pdftoppm and read by tesseract 5.5.0 (language eng, page segmentation mode 6), with only well-formed CM/ECF page-header stamps and bare page-number lines removed. The OCR text is not corrected by hand; quotations skip OCR errors (stray '|' marks, misread stamps) with '...'. Its spans point to src:<case_id>, the published OCR text.

R12 (rule own_systems_exclusion). Where an order's definition of an AI tool leaves out software that operates entirely on systems the party controls with no material sent to any third party, setup A (run on a party-controlled server, no outside provider) is outside the clause and is coded permitted, and self-hosting is named. Written while coding, after the frame was read.

replace.note: R10, R11, R12. Differs from the S.D.N.Y. template the posts group it with: its AI-tool definition leaves out software that runs entirely on the defense's own systems (and routine office features), it bars 'consumer (i.e., non-commercial)' versions rather than 'publicly accessible' ones, and it lets the defense use an AI tool once counsel has taken reasonable steps to confirm four safeguards, including that the tool permits deletion. Setup A is outside the clause; it would also meet the four safeguards.
